A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TSFM representation and steering work, despite the changed title and expanded scope. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-data experiments on MOMENT, including layer separability, steering outputs, alternative interventions, and generalization to different input trends (Figures 3–14).

after.justification: v3 reports original representation-similarity analyses, pruning evaluations, synthetic and ECG steering experiments, and downstream forecasting, imputation, classification, and anomaly-detection results.

M1.justification: v3 adds representation-guided block-wise pruning that preserves block endpoints and zeros intermediate layers (Algorithm 1), plus an optional block-identification algorithm (Algorithm 2). It also extends additive steering to combinations of trend and periodicity directions. These substantially expand v1's identification, localization, and steering pipeline.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates synthetic constant, sinusoidal, and triangular signals, including steering transfer to linear and exponential trends. v3 removes the triangular and exponential cases while adding explicit trend, periodicity, and amplitude discrimination, compositional steering, real-data forecasting and imputation, UCR classification and anomaly detection, and ECG5000 steering.

E2.justification: v3 adds unpruned controls for pruning and comparisons with methods including AnomalyTransformer, DGHL, GPT4TS, and TimesNet in Table 9, and TS2Vec, DTW, and ResNet in Table 11. v1's mean-based/LDA/SVM comparison for layer separability is no longer reported; the later SVM-based ECG experiment is a different comparison context.

E3.justification: v3 introduces multiple model families and sizes, four imputation masking rates, forecasting horizons, additional task metrics, and inference timing protocols. Table 6 specifies three training epochs and selection by best test-set performance. The reported synthetic configuration also changes: v1 Appendix B uses amplitude [-1,1] and period [128,164], whereas v3 Appendix A specifies amplitude 50 and period 128 for its seasonal cases.

E4.justification: v3 adds cross-size representation analyses, reported checks using cosine similarity and SVCCA, individual-block versus all-block pruning, compositional-steering sweeps, and an ECG case study. The intervention ablation changes from single versus all layers in v1 Figure 4 to single versus multiple tokens in v3 Figure 11. The original exponential-trend transfer analysis is removed.

E5.justification: v1 provides no explicit repeated-run or uncertainty reporting. v3 introduces five masking-seed runs with means and standard deviations (Tables 3 and 5), timing statistics from 100 passes (Table 7), and cross-dataset dispersion and correlation summaries (Tables 8 and 10). These are new reporting practices for the expanded evaluations.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive results absent from v1. Within its new pruning comparison, MOMENT's estimated size changes from 1301.76 to 615.76 MB and inference time from 20.88 to 19.82 ms (Table 7), while mean classification accuracy falls from 0.794 to 0.781 (Table 10). It also reports larger anomaly-detection losses and class changes for all 30 selected normal ECG samples after steering.

T1.justification: v3 adds a formal definition of contiguous redundant layer blocks and threshold-based identification conditions (Appendix C). Its mathematical signal specification is narrowed to affine and sinusoidal signals, replacing v1 Appendix A's broader waveform, exponential-trend, and noise definitions. Neither version develops theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v3 adds central claims about representation redundancy, model-size-dependent organization, and pruning that improves efficiency while maintaining accuracy. It reframes the contributions around cross-family representation analysis, concept identification, and compositional steering, substantially broadening v1's focus on synthetic concept localization and steering in MOMENT.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations connecting similarity blocks to redundant knowledge, explaining absent amplitude localization through normalization, and describing model-dependent steering calibration and excessive-steering failures. It also discusses practical applications and task-dependent pruning degradation. The limitation concerning transfer of synthetic steering matrices to real-world, out-of-distribution signals remains.

D1.justification: v3 adds code-access instructions, hardware specifications, model descriptions, exact visually selected pruning blocks, steering-strength guidance, and fine-tuning settings. Synthetic-data documentation is replaced with scenario-specific parameter ranges, although v1's explicit synthetic sample-count configuration is no longer supplied. These substantially change reproducibility information without establishing external resource availability.

R1.justification: v3 introduces a substantial representation-similarity and pruning literature discussion, including Kornblith, Raghu, Nguyen, and Phang, and positions its pruning approach relative to that work. It also expands TSFM coverage with newer scaling, long-context, and reasoning research, moving beyond v1's primarily concept-probing positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and methodological narrative are extensively rewritten around three contributions and seven research questions. v1's separate Setup section disappears, Future Work becomes part of Discussion and Limitations, and the appendices are reorganized. Reproducibility and impact statements are added.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main-text layout, redraws the methodology overview, and replaces or expands many original plots with pruning schematics, similarity heatmaps, token-level localization displays, and steering panels. It adds eleven tables and algorithm boxes, while removing the original synthetic-distribution histograms and triangular-pattern figures.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the empirical grounding and reproducibility of v1's single-model, mainly graphical synthetic study. Cross-family analyses are connected to controlled pruning evaluations with quantified accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs, repeated-seed results, and downstream failure cases. Expanded steering experiments and implementation disclosures add practical value. Table 6's test-set-based epoch selection and broad accuracy-preservation claims despite anomaly-detection losses weaken parts of the argument, but do not outweigh the substantial gains in validation and transparency.
